```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
# A gain-factor moderation variant (#391 finding 3) presents NO causal
# coefficient: its treatment term and interactions are explicitly associational,
# and the randomised headline lives in the interaction-free primary. Every
# causal-framing sentence in this partial branches on that flag so a variant
# report cannot contradict its own status.
_mv = bool((config.get("resolved_run_plan") or {}).get("moderation_variant", False))
if _mv:
    print(
        "This **moderation variant** reports **no causal coefficient**. It refits "
        "the outcome's gain-factor model with the pre-specified treatment "
        "interactions (on-intervention × ability, on-intervention × own baseline) "
        "restored, to ask whether the on-intervention association varies with those "
        "moderators. The interactions are estimated on **all** stacked periods — "
        "including post-crossover transitions with no untreated comparison — so "
        "every treatment-related quantity here, the netted marginal included, is a "
        "**model-dependent adjusted association**, partly informed by "
        "post-crossover data. Read the randomised causal headline from the "
        "interaction-free primary model this varies. Under the revised DAG "
        "(2026-07-10) every other coefficient is likewise an adjusted association: "
        "confounded by latent general ability, which the child random intercept "
        "does **not** control. Read them as *associated with*, never *drives*.\n\n"
        "_In plain terms:_ this companion asks whether the intervention's link with "
        "the outcome looks different for children with different starting points or "
        "ability. Because part of that evidence comes from after the comparison "
        "group had crossed over to the intervention, none of it counts as "
        "cause-and-effect; the main model carries the causal result."
    )
else:
    print(
        "The factor model reports **one** causal coefficient — the randomised "
        "on-intervention / t2 group contrast — alongside a vector of *adjusted "
        "associations*. Under the revised DAG (2026-07-10) every non-randomised "
        "coefficient is an adjusted association: it is confounded by latent general "
        "ability, and the child random intercept is only a partial, shrunken "
        "stand-in for between-child heterogeneity — **not** a control for that "
        "ability. Read them as *associated with*, never *drives*.\n\n"
        "_In plain terms:_ this section reports one effect the study can call "
        "causal — the group difference created by randomising who received the "
        "intervention — plus a set of side-by-side relationships (associations) "
        "between skills that the design cannot untangle from underlying ability."
    )
```

```{python}
    _lv = factor_summary[factor_summary.role == "levels_view"]
    print("### Baseline balance and the per-wave levels view\n")
    if len(_bal):
        _b = _bal.iloc[0]
        print(
            f"**Baseline balance — `{_b.term}`:** the covariate-adjusted "
            f"immediate-minus-waitlist difference at **t1**, before anyone was treated: "
            f"posterior median {_b['median']:+.3f} logits "
            f"(89% {_b['lo']:+.3f} to {_b['hi']:+.3f}; P(> 0) = {_b.prob_positive:.3f}). "
            "This is a **chance quantity** under randomisation — it exists because the "
            "model adjusts for age and ability at every wave and the arms differ "
            "slightly on both — and it is reported with its own prior as a *balance* "
            "term, **never as an effect**. The randomised contrast above is the change "
            "from this gap to the t2 gap, so whatever this gap is, it is subtracted out.\n"
        )
    if len(_lv):
        _cols = [c for c in ["term", "median", "lo", "hi", "prob_positive"] if c in _lv.columns]
        print(
            "**Per-wave arm gaps (levels view)** — the derived adjusted arm difference at "
            "each wave, `b_grp_time[t] = arm_gap_t1 + d_grp_time[t]` (t1 is the balance "
            "term itself). These are kept so the raw per-wave gaps can still be read — "
            "`b_grp_time[1]` is the raw adjusted t2 gap the pre-#552 parameterisation "
            "reported as its headline — but **none of them is the causal estimand**: "
            "the t2 row still carries the t1 chance imbalance, and the t3/t4 rows are "
            "post-crossover.\n"
        )
        print(_lv[_cols].to_markdown(index=False))
        print("")
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
# Level family only: the group contribution at t2 is
# (focal t2 term + gamma_grp_ability*ability)*G, but the causal card deliberately adds
# back only the focal term — gamma_grp_ability is a single *time-invariant* coefficient,
# identified from all four timepoints, three of which are not randomised, so folding it
# in would import a non-randomised component into a causal claim (#271 item 5; design
# note Decision 4). That makes the estimand "at mean ability", which the reader has to
# be told (#389 finding 1). Gated on the term's presence, so a level model fitted
# without group x ability prints nothing.
if (
    factor_summary is not None
    and "term" in factor_summary.columns
    and (factor_summary.term == "gamma_grp_ability").any()
):
    print(
        "_What the causal effect holds fixed:_ this model also carries a "
        "**group × ability** term, so the full group contribution at t2 is "
        f"`{_focal} + gamma_grp_ability × ability`"
        + (" (plus the t1 balance term `arm_gap_t1`, which is in both arms' prediction and is not part of the effect)" if _lf_t1 else "")
        + ". The effect reported above and "
        f"in the items-scale card below adds back **only `{_focal}`**: every child "
        "keeps their own baseline, but each receives the *same* group increment. The "
        "headline is therefore the average effect **at mean ability** — neither a "
        "population-average effect that lets the benefit vary with ability, nor a "
        "prediction for a single average-ability child. `gamma_grp_ability` is one "
        "*time-invariant* coefficient identified from all four timepoints, three of "
        "them not randomised, so folding it into the causal card would import a "
        "non-randomised component; it is reported on its own row above, as an adjusted "
        "association. See `notes/202606261230-gain-level-factors-design.md` Decision 4."
    )
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
# Items-scale treatment effect (gain family) and the on-intervention forest.
# Off-floor (Bernoulli) fits compute the same marginal with n_trials = 1, so the
# `trt_items_*` columns hold a RISK DIFFERENCE on the off-floor probability:
# render it in percentage points, never as "items" (gain-factors code review
# 2026-08-20, finding 1 — the level family never writes this CSV, so the branch
# only ever fires for gain fits, whose plan always carries `off_floor`).
treatment_marginal = _csv("treatment_marginal.csv")
_gf_off = bool(_plan.get("off_floor", False))


def _tm_value(v):
    if _gf_off:
        # round() first so a hair-negative value cannot render as "-0"; `or 0.0`
        # maps the rounded -0 back to +0 (the key-findings-builder idiom).
        return f"{round(float(v) * 100.0) or 0.0:+.0f}"
    return f"{float(v):+.1f}"


_tm_scale_name = "risk-difference" if _gf_off else "items"
_tm_unit = (
    "percentage points** on the chance of being off the floor at the period end"
    if _gf_off
    else "items**"
)
if treatment_marginal is not None:
    _t = treatment_marginal.iloc[0]
    _tm_band = (
        f"(50% CrI {_tm_value(_t.trt_items_lo50)} to {_tm_value(_t.trt_items_hi50)}; "
        f"89% {_tm_value(_t.trt_items_lo)} to {_tm_value(_t.trt_items_hi)})"
    )
    if _mv:
        print(
            f"On the {_tm_scale_name} scale, netting the fitted treatment interactions out of "
            f"`beta_trt` and averaging over the period-1 rows gives a median of "
            f"**{_tm_value(_t.trt_items_median)} {_tm_unit} "
            f"{_tm_band}; "
            f"P(> 0) = {_t.prob_trt_pos:.3f}. Because the netted interactions are "
            f"estimated on all stacked periods, this marginal is **model-dependent "
            f"and partly informed by post-crossover data** — it is *not* "
            f"exclusively randomised period-1 evidence, and the causal headline "
            f"lives in the interaction-free primary model.\n"
        )
    else:
        print(
            f"On the {_tm_scale_name} scale the treatment average marginal effect — averaged over the "
            f"**period-1 (randomised) transition only**, the genuinely all-untreated-baseline "
            f"contrast that defines this available-case modified ITT estimate — is a median of "
            f"**{_tm_value(_t.trt_items_median)} {_tm_unit} "
            f"{_tm_band}; "
            f"P(> 0) = {_t.prob_trt_pos:.3f}. The logit-scale `beta_trt` coefficient itself is "
            f"the on-intervention log-odds contrast, not the marginal available-case modified ITT estimate.\n"
        )
print(
    _img(
        "tau_forest.png",
        "Posterior of the on-intervention term (forest, reference line at 0) — a model-dependent association in this moderation variant"
        if _mv
        else (
            "Posterior of the t1 balance term and the per-wave arm-gap changes (forest, reference line at 0) — only the t2 change is randomised"
            if _lf_t1
            else "Posterior of the causal term (forest, reference line at 0)"
        ),
    )
)
print("\n_How to read the forest plot:_ the marker is the posterior median and the lines its credible intervals (thick = inner 50%, thin = 89%). The dashed line at 0 is no-effect; posterior mass to its right favours benefit, to its left harm; a wider line means more uncertainty.")
```

```{python}
# Group score trajectory — emitted for the level-factors (per-arm, per-timepoint)
# models only; the gain-factors family fits transitions and does not produce it, so
# the heading prints only when the figure exists.
if _has("group_trajectory.png"):

    print(_img("group_trajectory.png", "Per-arm score trajectory across waves, with credible ribbons and observed arm means"))
    print(
        f"\n_How to read it:_ each line is the model's posterior **mean** score on {outcome_label} "
        "for one randomised arm across the assessment waves (t1–t4), with its 89% credible ribbon; "
        "the filled dots are the observed per-arm means. This is a **population-level** curve — the "
        "child random intercept is integrated over its population distribution and the result is "
        "averaged over the children observed in each arm at each wave (g-computation). It is therefore "
        "a *different distribution* from the per-child panels below, which are conditional on each "
        "child's own fitted intercept; the two must not be read as the same thing. **Only the t2 gap "
        "is a randomised contrast.** The wait-list arm crosses to the intervention after t2, so the "
        "t3 and t4 separation is trajectory divergence under crossover, not a randomised effect."
    )
```

```{python}
# Adjusted associations, clearly fenced (METHODS.md causal-vs-association discipline).
# The level model's balance term and derived levels view (#552) carry their own roles
# and are reported in their own block above, not as associations.
if factor_summary is not None and "role" in factor_summary.columns:
    _assoc = factor_summary[~factor_summary.role.isin(["causal", "balance", "levels_view"])]
    if len(_assoc):
        _cols = [c for c in ["term", "median", "lo", "hi", "prob_positive"] if c in _assoc.columns]
        print('::: {.callout-important title="Adjusted associations — not causal"}\n')
        print(
            "Under the revised DAG (2026-07-10) every coefficient below is an adjusted "
            "association confounded by latent general ability — which the child random "
            "intercept does **not** control (it only absorbs between-child heterogeneity up "
            "to shrinkage) — and, for the level model, by the post-crossover cohort/timing "
            "structure after t2. Read as *associated with*, never *drives*.\n"
        )
        print(_assoc[_cols].to_markdown(index=False))
        print("\n:::")
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
# SP / RW baseline-timing note (#389 finding 5). Speech accuracy (deapp_c) and
# phonological memory (erbto) are read at the child's BASELINE (t1) value so the
# randomised contrast is not conditioned on a treatment-affected descendant (#247
# timing); their coefficients are therefore baseline-predictor associations, not
# contemporaneous per-wave factors. Term-gated, so it prints only where such an
# adjuster is actually in the summary (and stays silent for models without one).
if factor_summary is not None and "term" in factor_summary.columns:
    _terms = set(factor_summary["term"].astype(str))
    _baseline_adj = {
        "gamma_deapp_c": "speech accuracy",
        "gamma_erbto": "phonological memory (nonword repetition)",
    }
    _present = [lbl for t, lbl in _baseline_adj.items() if t in _terms]
    if _present:
        _names = " and ".join(_present)
        _plural = len(_present) > 1
        # Hearing is the contrasting case, so only mention it where it is actually
        # one of this model's adjusters.
        _hearing = (
            " Hearing, being exogenous, is read contemporaneously instead."
            if "gamma_hs" in _terms
            else ""
        )
        print(
            f"\n_Timing of the {_names} adjuster{'s' if _plural else ''}:_ read at "
            f"the child's **baseline (t1)** value — so the randomised contrast is not "
            f"conditioned on a treatment-affected descendant of the intervention "
            f"(#247 timing) — {'these are' if _plural else 'so this is a'} "
            f"**baseline-predictor association{'s' if _plural else ''}** applied "
            f"across all of a child's observations, **not** "
            f"{'contemporaneous per-wave factors' if _plural else 'a contemporaneous per-wave factor'}."
            f"{_hearing}"
        )
```

```{python}
# Items-scale association marginals (#310): the interpretable companion to the
# logit-scale adjusted associations above. For each covariate, the average marginal
# effect of a +1 SD perturbation (and, for the bounded-count baselines, a +k-items
# one) on the outcome, averaged over ALL fitted rows. Every row is an association.
association_marginals = _csv("association_marginals.csv")
if association_marginals is not None and len(association_marginals):
    _am = association_marginals
    _off = bool(_am["off_floor"].iloc[0]) if "off_floor" in _am.columns else False
    _unit = "off-floor probability" if _off else "items"
    print('::: {.callout-important title="Items-scale associations — not causal"}\n')
    print(
        f"Each row translates one adjusted-association coefficient onto an interpretable "
        f"scale: the average marginal effect on **{outcome_label}** of a +1 SD increase in "
        f"the covariate (and, for the bounded-count baselines, a reader-friendly +5-items "
        f"increase), averaged over **all fitted rows** — the descriptive averaging "
        f"population, in contrast to the treatment marginal's randomised period-1 rows. "
        f"These are the same adjusted associations as the logit table above, so every row "
        f"is *associated with*, never *drives*"
        + (
            " — and for this floored outcome the effect is a change in the probability of "
            "being off the floor, not an item count."
            if _off
            else "."
        )
        + "\n"
    )
    _assoc_cols = [
        c
        for c in ["term", "scale", "items_median", "items_lo", "items_hi", "prob_pos", "sd_items"]
        if c in _am.columns
    ]
    print(_am[_assoc_cols].round(3).to_markdown(index=False))
    print(
        f"\n_How to read it:_ `items_median` is the {_unit} change (best single estimate), "
        f"`items_lo`/`items_hi` its 89% credible interval, `prob_pos` the posterior "
        f"probability the association is positive, and `sd_items` (bounded-count "
        f"covariates only) how many items a +1 SD move is at the mean baseline — so "
        f"\"+1 SD\" can be read back in items."
    )
    print("\n:::")
```
